title: Keep UVC webcams at a fixed frame rate
head: fd16f40ed292
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Absent or compound capability metadata silently excludes a UVC capture node
leads.consequence: If v4l_id cannot open/query a node, ID_V4L_CAPABILITIES is absent; if a capture device reports another v4l_id category as well, its string is not exactly :capture:. Either event skips this rule's RUN without any diagnostic from this rule, even if it is a UVC capture node; v4l_id itself can warn when its open fails. Whether either case occurs on a particular supported camera remains untested; this is a verified conditional input boundary, not evidence that the author's two tested cameras are affected. A control absent from a successfully matched camera is likewise silently swallowed by the deliberate || : guard; this should be described as unsupported rather than a guaranteed fixed frame rate.
leads.triage: contradicted_dropped; coordinator read: uvcvideo sets capture device_caps to VIDEO_CAPTURE|STREAMING only (uvc_driver.c:2061-2070) and v4l_id uses device_caps when DEVICE_CAPS is set, so compound strings do not arise for uvcvideo; absent-property case (v4l_id open failure) is an unevidenced edge; Opus final item 2 agrees

leads.summary: v4l2-ctl is not a dependency of the package that ships this udev rule
leads.consequence: On a minimal or modified installation without v4l-utils, every otherwise matching RUN returns success but does not change the camera, since /usr/bin/v4l2-ctl is missing and its shell error goes to /dev/null. The standard install currently includes mpv, whose Arch dependency ffmpeg depends on v4l-utils, so this is NOT a claim that a normal freshly installed desktop lacks it. To make the new package-owned rule independent of that unrelated transitive chain, add 'v4l-utils' after 'plymouth' in both omarchy-settings depends lists (stable PKGBUILD line 44; dev PKGBUILD line 35).
leads.triage: already_in_opus_final; corroborates Opus F4; coordinator verified PKGBUILD depends list and etc/ copy; published as Optional note

leads.summary: The static test does not ensure its match predicates and RUN belong to one effective rule
leads.consequence: A syntactically valid edit adding an unsatisfiable condition (for instance ENV{OMARCHY_NEVER_SET}=="yes") to the matched line, or moving RUN onto a separate nonmatching rule, can leave every grep and udevadm verify assertion passing while the webcam never receives the control change. This is a test-coverage gap, not evidence that the rule in the pinned head fails. Assert all required tokens share one effective rule and add a negative regression for an extra exclusion, rather than treating independent text searches or a syntax verifier as behavioural coverage.
leads.triage: confirmed_by_inspection_not_published; true by inspection of independent grep checks; not executed as a mutant; public test note limited to demonstrated m8 and skip convention

limits: Source-only boundary hunt at fd16f40ed292fd1bdcd74a05c30e0fb9f312bb7e. No camera or udev daemon was reserved, so no hardware control write, host trigger, or runtime test was performed.

Arch package metadata and systemd v262 were read at review time, not pinned distribution snapshots for Omarchy 4.0.3/4.0.4; the code-path claims rely on cited source, but versions may differ on older installations.

Related open PRs #12972 (USB-interface camera disable), #13019 (camera busy widget), and #11652 (Intel IPU6 via relay) have no demonstrated conflicting change to this rule or test. #12972 disables the interface before video nodes appear and re-enables it by re-probing, so subsequent node-add events should still reach this rule; no device experiment confirms timing.
No upstream browser application behavior was verified as part of this boundary hunt; main-logic and resume behavior are reserved to the full reviewer.

flags.claim: Chromium comparison: ResetUserAndCameraControlsToDefault() runs on every start and sets the control to QUERYCTRL's default
flags.why: The function is called on every AllocateAndStart, but it first sets V4L2_CID_AUTO_WHITE_BALANCE and returns before touching AE priority if that S_CTRL fails after 5 retries. It is also only Chromium's V4L2 capture path; the PipeWire camera path (WebRtcPipeWireCamera, not enabled in Omarchy's config/chromium-flags.conf today; proposed in open PR #11053) does not run it. My own final.md (item 9, F1) missed the early return.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; Chromium row now: every V4L2 capture start, once its auto-white-balance reset succeeds

flags.claim: Chromium's reset always lands on 0 on UVC cameras
flags.why: It lands on 0 whenever the reset reaches the AE-priority step, because uvcvideo always reports default 0 for this control. But the reset is skipped on cameras whose auto-white-balance set fails, and it only runs on Chromium's V4L2 capture path. "always" is too strong.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; 'whenever Chromium's V4L2 reset runs, it lands on 0'

flags.claim: so today mpv, OBS and Firefox see a different rate depending on whether a Chromium-based app opened the camera since boot
flags.why: Several qualifiers are missing. (1) The rate difference only appears in light dim enough for AE priority to stretch exposure, and only on cameras that start with the control on. (2) OBS writes camera controls from its V4L2 source properties dialog, so it is not purely passive (my final.md H3). (3) Electron apps are assumed to use the same Chromium V4L2 path; I did not verify that. (4) The C8 early return applies. "see" should be "can see".
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; dim light, camera starting with control on, 'can', since plugged in; OBS dropped

flags.why: The rule comment does not repeat the descriptor claim, but it does say "Chromium turns it off on every open; mpv, OBS and Firefox never touch it". Chromium's reset can return early (C8), and OBS can write controls from its properties dialog (C14). The other comment statements are accurate: metadata node without controls, failed RUN logging, sort order.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; 'the rule's comment does not make this claim'

flags.claim: checking for /usr/bin/v4l2-ctl, $devnode, the control assignment and the || : guard separately would keep the intent without pinning the exact text
flags.why: This is internally inconsistent with the example one sentence earlier. A separate check for the control assignment (`exposure_dynamic_framerate=0`) would still reject the numeric-ID rewrite `--set-ctrl 0x009a0903=0` (mutant m8) given as the behaviour-preserving false failure. Separate checks only remove brittleness to layout, such as argument order, spacing and where `2>/dev/null` sits.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; now says separate checks stop pinning layout and would still reject numeric-ID form

flags.claim: so the cost is per-event overhead rather than touching unrelated devices
flags.why: This drops a qualifier from my report (final.md F3: "per-event overhead plus setting the control on any V4L node of any driver"). v4l2-ctl stops only for non-V4L2 nodes. On every event of any V4L2 node (non-UVC cameras, v4l2loopback, capture cards, sub-devices), it would open the node, enumerate controls and set the control where it exists. Those are devices outside the rule's UVC scope.
flags.disposition: real_error_fixed; restored qualifier: set attempt on every V4L2 node of any driver

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** checked against the systemd, uvcvideo (Linux 7.2.7), v4l-utils 1.32.0 and Chromium sources, the rule does what the description says. No correctness issue was found in the rule. The notes below concern one rationale in the PR description, the new test, and an optional layout change.

| Claim | Source check |
|---|---|
| Match properties are set before position 65 | `60-persistent-v4l.rules` imports `v4l_id` and `usb_id`; `ID_USB_DRIVER` is the parent interface driver (`uvcvideo`) |
| Capture nodes only | uvcvideo gives capture nodes `VIDEO_CAPTURE\|STREAMING` and the metadata node `META_CAPTURE\|STREAMING`; `v4l_id` reads `device_caps` and has no meta token, so capture is exactly `:capture:` and metadata is `:` |
| Boot and hot-plug | coldplug in `systemd-udev-trigger.service` uses `--action=add` |
| Quiet journal | udev logs a nonzero RUN exit as a warning but RUN stderr only at debug level, so `\|\| :` is what suppresses the warning |
| Control name | current uvcvideo uses the framework name "Exposure, Dynamic Framerate", which `v4l2-ctl` maps to `exposure_dynamic_framerate` (Linux 5.15 still used "Auto Priority") |
| Chromium comparison | `ResetUserAndCameraControlsToDefault()` runs on every V4L2 capture start and, once its auto-white-balance reset succeeds, sets the control to `QUERYCTRL`'s default |

A sandboxed run of the new test passed all 9 checks. The rule's inner command, run through `/bin/sh -c` with a stub for `v4l2-ctl`, exited 0 with no stderr when the stub failed, succeeded, or was missing.

### The `default=0` rationale does not come from the camera

The description says the camera's descriptor reports the control as off by default and the firmware boots it on. In uvcvideo, the AE-priority entry in `uvc_ctrls[]` (`drivers/media/usb/uvc/uvc_ctrl.c`) has `SET_CUR | GET_CUR | RESTORE` and no `UVC_CTRL_FLAG_GET_DEF`. `GET_DEF` is only sent and `default_value` only filled when that flag is set, so `v4l2-ctl` shows `default=0` for this control on every UVC camera, whatever the device reports.

**Impact:** the 1 the cameras boot with is the vendor's power-on setting. The rule overrides that choice rather than correcting a descriptor mismatch. The same fact supports the Chromium comparison: whenever Chromium's V4L2 reset runs, it lands on 0 on UVC cameras and nothing restores the old value on stop. So today, on a camera that starts with the control on, mpv and Firefox can run at a different rate in dim light depending on whether Chromium opened the camera since it was plugged in.

**Suggested change:** reword the description (the rule's comment does not make this claim) to describe the rule as a policy override of the firmware's power-on value.

### Optional test improvement

- When `udevadm verify` is unavailable, the check is dropped without output. `docs/testing.md` asks for `skip "…"` with a reason so the runner lists it; an `else skip "udevadm verify is unavailable"` branch would do that.
- The check on line 44 pins the whole `RUN+=` string. In a mutation run it failed a behaviour-preserving rewrite (`--set-ctrl 0x009a0903=0`), and removing the `|| :` guard was caught by this check before the dedicated guard check could run. `docs/testing.md` asks to "Assert the invariant, not the snapshot": checking for `/usr/bin/v4l2-ctl`, `$devnode`, the control assignment and the `|| :` guard separately would keep the intent without pinning the command's layout (a separate check for `exposure_dynamic_framerate=0` would still reject the numeric-ID form).

### Optional: a single-line rule avoids a partial comment-out trap

udev drops a `#` line without looking at its trailing backslash. If someone disables the rule by commenting out only line 9 (a local edit that the companion `backup=` change in omacom/omarchy-pkgs#664 makes expected), line 10 becomes a `RUN+=` rule with no match keys. It then runs `/bin/sh` and `v4l2-ctl` on every uevent, and `udevadm verify` accepts that file. `v4l2-ctl` exits before opening non-V4L2 devices, so the cost is per-event overhead plus a set attempt on every V4L2 node of any driver. Writing the match keys and `RUN+=` on one line removes the trap.

```text
# ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="video4linux", ... \     <- commented out
  RUN+="/bin/sh -c '...v4l2-ctl...'"                 <- now a rule of its own, matches every uevent
```

**Optional:** `omarchy-settings` ships the rule but does not depend on `v4l-utils`, and `|| :` also hides a missing `/usr/bin/v4l2-ctl`. On the default package set `v4l-utils` arrives through `mpv` → `ffmpeg` and through `obs-studio`, so this only matters for trimmed installs. A direct `v4l-utils` dependency would make the rule self-contained.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the rule and test against systemd v261/v262, Linux v7.2.7 uvcvideo, v4l-utils 1.32.0, Chromium `v4l2_capture_delegate.cc`, Firefox's vendored libwebrtc, FFmpeg n9.0.2 and the omarchy-pkgs PKGBUILDs. The new test, `udevadm verify` and a mutation matrix ran in a sandbox. No camera hardware or live udev daemon was used. Matching, boot, hot-plug and suspend behaviour rest on source and the author's live report. The brightness trade-off was not measured.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
